citations.review_text: best game ever takes a bit to get into but is a great game
Really fun game. Lots of exploring, first hour a little underwhelming but it gets better

The first hour is more or less a strange introduction from what i remember, past that it's fun.,.
[h2] HOWEVER... [/h2]
I'm not going to pretend the game is perfect, even in the little time I've played it I've seen some issues.
Sometimes, the shadow you leave behind when you die is impossible to reach. I once lost two hours of money buildup because of that. The game is difficult and you will lose a couple hour's worth of money here and there and that's OK, it's just that you can sometimes lose progress to bugs like that.
A far larger and more pervasive issue is; if you dont have the layout memorized, expect to have half your time playing the game being a walking/mild parkour simulator to get from boss A to boss B while fighting a miniboss or two inbetween. This is not as much of a problem as in other games because you get to explore different biomes on the way, but the novelty of the new biomes wears off after exploring it three to four times back-to-back because you have no idea where to go.
I consider the walking sim aspect of this game to be the worst part of the game so far, but that doesn't mean those parts are the worst things to ever be created in the history of video games. I just think that where you should go should be more clear. One way would be to probably have all of the progression in one direction, instead of fighting a boss on the left side of the map, running to the right side of the map to fight another boss, and going further down to continue progression just to do the same thing.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the early game is slow and can leave new players lost or unsure of where to go before opening up later.

citations.review_text:
Hollow Knight is one of the most wonderful games I have ever played. It has a well-written story with a perfect way of telling it through its characters. The way they connected the whole world together is truly brilliant and really amazes me. The graphics are great and suit the world's dark atmosphere, with beautiful places to explore.
However, Hollow Knight has some problems, especially with the bosses. The bosses are really hard to defeat. And I am not talking about a normal difficulty (or fair difficulty) that exists in other bosses in other games, such as Cuphead. The problem with Hollow Knight's bosses is that sometimes you cannot avoid getting hit. In games Like Cuphead, you can avoid the attacks if you are fast enough or clever enough, but in Hollow Knight, sometimes the bosses do not give you any chance to escape or avoid the damage, even if you are fast. I consider this to be unfair difficulty. 
Moreover, The game is ambiguous and does not give you enough hints about where to go. I know that this thing is made to encourage you to explore the map, but when I first played the game, I really did not know what I was supposed to do or where I was supposed to go. Every time I tried to leave the Forgotten Crossroads I face something preventing me from reaching other area, such as the creature blocking the entrance to Greenpath. This made me try the game three times before finally playing it long enough to understand what I was supposed to do. 
The problems that I mentioned may not actually be problems, because Hollow knight is a souls-like game after all, and maybe these things are normal for this type of game.  I do not really know, I did not play souls game before. 
Despite these problems, Hollow Knight has a great story with good characters and wonderful map, which makes you addicted to the game. It is a true masterpiece, and I recommend everyone to play it.

All I've heard is that this game is a masterpiece, and yet no one can tell me exactly what makes this game a masterpiece. After beating path of pain and played the grand majority of bosses excluding absolute radiance and hornet nosk, hollow knight is a good game, just not a masterpiece.

* Pacing is slow at the beginning and doesn't hook newcomers early
* Aspect ratio is too big for certain areas like the descend to city of tears, even though the enemy AI is great, it gives the player too much room and it doesn't make them feel like opponents blocking your path.
* Pacing is inconsistent across the whole game. If it's soul sanctum with the two toads guarding the top, it's good. If it's forgotten crossroads, it's bad. 
* bosses are overall good, some of them were the highlights of the game (soul tyrant, white defender, NKG, mantis lords or sisters of battle, lost kin) but some are either a snoozefest (uumuu or flukewarm) or do something that ruins the experience (pure vessel/NKG to a lesser extent and the 2 mask contact/stunned damage)
* I don't really consider this game as a metroidvania since it doesn't really have some of the more intrinsic things you see in a castlevania game, or fully understanding what makes metroid metroid. I'd say this is an action platformer, with paper mario badges, and some elements of metroid and dark souls sprinkled on there without fully realizing what made those game what they are. The thing about metroid is that reverse boss order runs are a pretty common thing in their speedrun community, which means you not only need to have a better understanding of the game, but the toolkit samus has needs to be designed to where she can do this. All of the upgrades metroid offers are there, but since samus has depth to her moveset, skilled players can progress through a level with the tools she has. The knight has no depth aside from unlocking the upgrades, which can discourage newcomers from playing the game on repeat agai…

I bought this game years ago. I loved all the Dark Souls games, and I enjoyed the art style. I started it multiple times but never got that far. I had never played a Metroidvania before, so I was constantly getting lost and was overwhelmed by the size of the map.

Years later, after playing multiple Metroid games, I felt ready to come back to Hollow Knight. I unlocked the map, bought the Wayward Compass charm so I could see myself on it, and started playing. No longer getting lost, I was able to progress and enjoy the game.

The art, music, and atmosphere is amazing. I was fully immersed, and was surprised how emotionally invested I was in the world and characters. The controls are incredibly responsive, and while simple at first by the end I felt like I had mastered them. It felt great returning to areas that had destroyed me in the beginning, we now easy to breeze by hours later. The combat is a lot of fun, and while I could beat a lot of bosses first try, there were many that required me to learn their patterns before I could stand a chance.

I think it is easy to set limitations upon ourselves when it comes to harder games. I thought I was not good enough to complete a lot of the content, or that I would not have the time to get better. But by allowing ourselves to fail and learn from our mistakes, we can beat those challenges we first thought were impossible. Just like the story of Hollow Knight, we are always capable of more.

Goated game!

The only bad thing I noticed is that the pacing at the beginning is a bit slow. I personally didn’t really mind it, though. I’ve heard other people complain about it, but once you get past the slow start and really get into the flow of the game, you’ll love it.

If you haven’t given the game a shot yet, I definitely recommend doing so. The runbacks can be pretty awful at times, but most of the bosses are really fun to fight. Either that, or I just first-tried them, so I didn’t notice the runbacks as much.

Overall, it’s just a beautiful game. The art style looks amazing, the animations are incredibly smooth, and the soundtrack is so good that I actually listen to it in my free time. The world-building is also fantastic, and the story and lore are really interesting especially that you have to kinda figure out whats going on in this world.

Definitely a game I’d recommend giving a chance (more than just 3 hours of gameplay).

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the White Palace is a mandatory, grueling, and unforgiving platforming-only area that serves as a severe difficulty spike near the end of the game.

citations.review_text: Hollow Knight is a game with really high highs and really low lows. It handles exploration really well and a lot of the base combat is actually really enjoyable. It has a lot of elements that i like but at the same time it has some design choices that puzzle me and ultimately ruined the game for me. i have over 130 hours in the game and a lot of my time was spent exploring but once I got to the white palace all of the enjoyment was sapped from me. In the most puzzling of decisions they made that specific MANDATORY area the most grueling and unforgiving stage that i've ever had the displeasure of playing in. It made me quit on a game that i was enjoying pretty well up till that part which is telling on how bad it is. Team Cherry has some genuinely talented minds when it comes to game design, its just decisions like this that make me never want to finish their games fully. Its not a design flaw, its a design decision where they knowingly make stages that are just insane difficulty spikes. Sucks all the enjoyment out of what is otherwise a solid game.

After playing the game for a while now, my main file only having Pantheon 5 left, Mr.Mushroom, and some miscellaneous things to finish up, I can say this is still a game worth trying after so much time. Now that Silksong has been out for a while and got the well-deserved hype, Hollow Knight is still something to get a footing in. 112% sounds scary, but by the time you unlock the % dial, you'll have most of the things you need and know what is missing. 

Platforming, overall, is fun and enjoyable. Mixed with combat that utilizes the environment in a satisfying way. The only time I did not enjoy this game was White Palace, a platforming-only section of Hollow Knight end game. While the first few sections were fine, albeit frustrating, the ending section before *lore* was the only time I really did not want to play the game. 

Outside of that, this is a 9/10 game. Implied lore that you need to piece together yourself, with the different endings and unique fights, makes this a game I come back to.
